question: Does plain ensembling (equal average of two seeds of the same model) reliably beat a single model?
disclosure: post hoc consistency check on already-scored test predictions; no training or selection; the holdout control already showed pairs about equal to the blend

cohorts.development: original 7 mice, frozen_retrieval saved test predictions, seeds 401-403

ensembles.pair: slot s = 0.5*clip(seed s)+0.5*clip(seed next(s)), next cyclic 401->402->403->401
ensembles.triple: equal average of all three seeds (one per mouse; descriptive)

comparator: single model of the same family; per-mouse seed-mean MSE for relative gains; seed-slot win = pair slot s beats single seed s
gate: per family and cohort: mean relative MSE gain>=5%, mouse wins>=ceil(6/7*n), slot wins>=ceil(2/3*3n), worst mouse harm<=10%, mean MAE gain>=0; also report active and quiet slices
input_checks: single-model MSE must match already-audited rows (bounded_hybrid summary.json, holdout summary.json) to 1e-12
